title: census.py summary prints the phase-2 reading queue's size and estimated tokens, and each census phase records an ops row with its wall time and counts
goal: census.py summary LOG adds a queue block computed with no network and no model: the rows phase 2 must read (bucket not OK, note not blocked, no outcome yet), the facts citing them (rag.py src --cited counts), the characters of their factdiff review passages and, for rows without review items, of the whole documents held in _cache/factdiff (a not-cached count when absent), and the tokens estimated at characters/4, split by provider host; census.py check, record and confirm and factdiff.py detect, apply and review each write one ops row census.phase (phase, date, ms, rows per bucket or outcome, exit) through ql_capture.record as tests.py writes test.run, and the digest's ops block counts them; the 2026-09-26 log's queue figure is recorded in kb/_self/reports/fact-diff.md as the census baseline.

gates.question: What shape does the ops row census.phase take, and when is it written? Recommended: keys phase, date (a new closed date shape), ms, exit and optional rows, a table of name and n (a lower-case token per bucket, verdict or outcome, zero counts left out); no row for a --dry-run; the digest's ops block gives the event's count, failures and median ms beside land.end, sync.gate and test.run.

How does the queue size one row phase 2 reads, and how is it split? Recommended: the passages of its fact diff review items (fact, old passage, new passage) when the fact diff log holds items for it, else its whole document in _cache/factdiff (the clone's main worktree cache when this worktree has none; not cached counts 0 characters and is counted); the split is by the host of the source url, naming the 15 hosts of most characters and one line for the rest.

How does census.py summary find the fact diff log whose review items it sizes? Recommended: an optional --factdiff FLOG, else the log the rows' evidence names (factdiff.py review NAME, beside LOG), else factdiff-<date of LOG>.csv beside LOG, else none (every row is sized as a whole document).

The suite is at the ceiling: 100 of 100 test ids, and its scenario of tests.py's reuse (test_sync_e2e.py) adds a stray test file to a clone, so a 15th tracked test file makes that scenario see 16 files and fail; a full run takes about 21 s against the darwin ceiling of 22 s. This story's checks need two test ids in one new file, _tools/test_census_route.py (the queue's sizing; the phases' ops rows with the digest line), so tests.py exits 1 with 102 ids and 15 files. Which makes room?

notes: Premise run 2026-10-10: python3 _tools/census.py summary kb/public/_census/2026-09-26.csv printed bucket, outcome and needs-reading-by-note counts and the confirmed count, and nothing about the size of what phase 2 reads (no facts, characters or tokens); no census.phase ops row exists (git grep census.phase in _tools finds nothing). This story sets the baseline the epic's later stories are measured against, so it lands first. Its test selector collects no test until the work adds _tools/test_census.py. The tokens estimate follows kb/_self/usage.md's characters/4 convention.
